pages.title: Terrain that stays joined
pages.subtitle: Cliff profiles, resident terrain boundaries and opaque chunk replacement.

images.caption: Before: repeated comb-like cliff projections in the matched canyon fixture.
After: the same cliff-field fixture with the artificial projections repaired.

blocks.heading: Actual neighbouring surfaces now meet
blocks.text: Terrain boundaries fit the profiles that are currently drawn. Missing river-bank profile knots are inserted into the affected boundary triangles, keeping movement/contact heights aligned. This closes the slits caused by mixing ready meshes with older or coarser neighbours.

Smooth mode moves one opaque mesh between heights on eligible distant, dry, unrooted leaf tiles. Shared boundaries remain fixed. Nearby interactive ground, refined rivers, ancestors with children and coarsening use immediate replacement. Native checks inspect actual height movement and perspective coverage.

pages.title: Water and woodland
pages.subtitle: Current native examples from generated reproduction worlds.

images.caption: Waterfall after the terrain/water repair. Final wide-world validation remains pending.

blocks.text: Water and terrain are reviewed together at steep reaches, including the ground beneath and beside the falls. The pictured case shows the current result; it is not evidence that every possible river has been inspected.

images.caption: Current fjord review with physical tree silhouettes at world scale.

blocks.text: Distant canopy colour uses crown coverage rather than stem occupancy, helping woodland read as woodland without adding trees or draw calls. The oversized distant-card representation has been replaced in the reviewed view.

The original world was unsaved, so testing uses generated reproductions. The cliff pair is matched; the other screenshots depict different locations and should not be read as a single continuous route.

pages.title: Performance and limits
pages.subtitle: Provisional comparison; the strict 100 FPS floor is still unmet.

blocks.text: Average speed improved substantially in this measured route, but long frames remain. These figures precede the final garbage-collection comparison and final horizon review. They do not establish a universal improvement or a 100 FPS minimum. Final accepted settings, workload and build association must accompany the published results.

blocks.heading: Preparation and streaming use separate clocks

blocks.text: The 8.8 s and 24.7 s milestones begin after preparation; they are not total time from entering the world. The final 191 km result is still pending. Grouped horizon fallbacks retain height/material sample spacing while reducing object counts, but their larger individual uploads also need checking.
